waivers.reason: Every remaining hit is the CARDINAL DETERMINER 'one' ('one hook', 'one revision row', 'one live run'), not a pronoun with an unclear referent. GTWR_R32 asks for 'each' over 'all/any/both' and this corpus obeys it; 'one' is the singular counterpart and its referent is the noun it modifies. The four genuine pronoun hits ('it', 'that') were rewritten rather than waived.

Two classes, neither indefinite. (a) 'as' in 'record X as Y' / 'return X as text' is the copular preposition, not a temporal keyword — the lexical scan cannot tell them apart. (b) 'before' / 'after' / 'latest' in EXE-6, EXE-7, EXE-8, EXE-9, EXE-19, EXE-26 and EXE-29 name a DEFINITE ordering that IS the requirement: worklog.py:126-133 appends before it awaits, and core.py:325 reads the cap off the latest verdict. R35 targets 'eventually'/'until'; no requirement here uses either.

Each hit is a single compound OBJECT, not two thoughts: 'the document text and the lineage together' is one digest input tuple (artifacts.py:435-450), 'each member and the lead' is one retire gather (core.py:277-281), the three identifiers in XPL-9 are one composite join key (org-plane.md:106-109), and 'one run or fewer' is one numeric bound. Splitting any of them would state something the code does not: the digest over content alone is a different function.

The lowercase 'and' sits in a PRECONDITION or TRIGGER slot where it conjoins genuinely separate guard conditions — ORG-14's release gate really is accepted-reviews AND zero-unresolved-conflicts AND divergence-not-confirmed (org-plane.md:101-105). symspec's own atomizer reads the slot text as prose, so adopting the bracketed [X AND Y] convention would change what the solver compares without changing what the gate means.

Both hits are correctly indefinite. EXE-23 refuses ANY in-memory database, not a particular one (trajectory.py:161 tests for two substrings). XPL-7 quantifies over any revision that carries a decides value (artifacts.py:182-185).

Every refinement leaf here carries verificationMethod plus a verificationNote naming the exact source file and line range, or the design-doc section, it was read off — which IS the independent verification obligation KAOS leaf-verifiability asks for. Adding a `verifies` EDGE would mean inventing verification requirements that restate the notes, growing the corpus without adding a claim.

Reviewed and DECLINED, class by class. The largest cluster is the nine org-plane transitions, which are deliberately distinct rows of one transition matrix — collapsing 'move to assigned' and 'move to running' onto one atom would make the matrix unprovable and would manufacture conflicts between legal transitions. The content-plane cluster ('advance main to the proposal revision' / 'to the seeded revision') names two genuinely different target revisions; merging them would prove a conflict the plane does not contain.
